title: iter-3 R3-002 (silent BigInt try/catch) FIXED — console.warn now fires on both paths
description: Verification of iter-4 fix for iter-3 R3-002 / iter-3 C008. The try/catch around BigInt(orderIdStr) now console.warns on BOTH the SyntaxError path (catch block) and the non-finite-coercion path (the `if (!Number.isFinite(price))` branch). Both warnings name the original orderIdStr and explain that the code is falling back to compute-time order_id decode. This addresses the silent-swallowing concern in iter-3 R3-002. No further action needed.
impact: Operator now sees a console.warn for the two failure modes that iter-3 silently masked. Confirmed fixed.
recommendation: None. Optionally upgrade to a counter that surfaces in PoolCardData (e.g. malformedOrderCount) so the UI can also reflect partial-data state, but that is a UX concern not an error-handling regression.

title: iter-3 R3-001 (wrong bit-127 mask) FIXED — both ask and bid prices now correct
description: Verification of iter-4 fix for iter-3 R3-001 / iter-3 R3-014 carry-over. The decode is now `Number((BigInt(orderIdStr) & ((1n<<127n)-1n)) >> 64n)`. The mask `(1n<<127n)-1n` is bit-127 = 0, bits 0..126 = 1 — correctly clearing the ask flag bit before extracting the high 64 bits of the remaining 127. Per synthesis-notes empirical verification (bid 12377783720203182843884075 → 671000, ask 170141183460486719245069180370816077150 → 948000), this matches captured-chain prices for both sides. The earlier inverted-bid concern (chain-shape.md prose) appears to be contradicted by the captured data and is acknowledged in the inline comment.
impact: R3-001 (iter-3) and R3-014 (iter-2) are now resolved. mid/spread/best-bid/best-ask render correctly against real chain data. Verified by reading the literal mask expression and the inline empirical comment.
recommendation: None. Two lingering concerns worth tracking but not raising as findings: (a) the 'no bid inversion' assertion contradicts notes/chain-shape.md prose — if a future pool encodes bids the inverted way, this decode silently produces garbage; (b) the inline comment is the ONLY record of the empirical verification — consider adding a unit test pinning these two captured order_ids → expected prices to make the regression visible.

title: iter-3 R3-016 (resolvePoolInnerFields null silently fabricates empty book) STILL PRESENT
description: Iter-4 did NOT touch fetchPoolStats's null-innerFields branch. Lines 380-385 still construct a hardcoded empty PoolInnerState with `{ asks: [], bids: [], lot_size: '0', ... }` whenever resolvePoolInnerFields returns null. resolvePoolInnerFields returns null at line 114 (no fields) and line 144 (no wrapperFields), and silently DEGRADES (returning the outer pool fields) at lines 121, 125, 134 — none of these paths surface to the user. The empty-book result then flows through computeMarketStats → all metrics undefined → PoolCard renders '—' for every value, indistinguishable from a healthy idle pool.
impact: Same as iter-3 R3-016: a pool object that's mid-upgrade, deleted, or whose wrapper shape has drifted produces '—' across the board with no operator-visible distinction from 'no orders on book'. AC1.1 'inline error UI' bypassed for this path. The fix log for iter-4 makes no mention of this finding, which was rated high in iter-3 — apparent regression of attention.
recommendation: Either throw with an actionable message ('Pool ${descriptor.poolId} inner state unreadable — wrapper shape mismatch') so the per-pool error banner fires, or attach a `dataState: 'ok' | 'partial' | 'empty' | 'error'` field to PoolCardData. At minimum, console.warn with the descriptor + the recovery path taken (matches the new iter-4 console.warn pattern in traverseBigVector).

title: rpc() still does not check response.ok; non-2xx → opaque JSON-parse error
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-006 / iter-2 R3-004. Iter-4 did not touch rpc(). `await response.json()` is still called with no `if (!response.ok)` guard. A 502/503 from the Sui RPC port, a 404 from a wrong path, or an HTML error page from a misconfigured proxy throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0` instead of the actionable RPC-unreachable error AC1.1/T-020 promises. With Promise.allSettled fan-out (App.tsx), this opaque error is multiplied N times in the alert banner — N copies of 'Unexpected token <' tells the operator nothing actionable.
impact: Sandbox-down or sandbox-restart-mid-cycle (a contract-acknowledged failure mode) surfaces as opaque JSON parse errors instead of an actionable 'Sui RPC unreachable; run pnpm deploy-all'.
recommendation: Before `await response.json()`: `if (!response.ok) throw new Error(\`Sui RPC ${method} returned HTTP ${response.status} from ${rpcUrl}. Verify the sandbox is running.\`);`. Wrap the json() call in try/catch too. Same fix shape that iter-4 applied to the BigInt try/catch should apply here.

title: rpc() still does not handle network-level fetch rejection (DNS, ECONNREFUSED)
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-007. fetch() has no try/catch; the most common sandbox-down case (port closed → `TypeError: Failed to fetch`) propagates verbatim. The error message names neither rpcUrl nor the bootstrap recipe. Worsened by iter-2's Promise.allSettled fan-out — the user sees one identical 'Failed to fetch' line per pool. Iter-4 did not address.
impact: The most user-visible failure mode (sandbox not running) gets the least actionable error. Multiplied by pool count in the App alert banner.
recommendation: Wrap fetch in try/catch and rethrow with an actionable message including rpcUrl and bootstrap hint, attaching the original via `{ cause: err }`.

title: rpc() still casts env.result to T without checking it is defined
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-008. `return env.result as T` proceeds even if env.result is undefined. Downstream callers read fields off undefined/empty objects via ?. and ?? defaults, silently producing empty books / no fills. Iter-4 unchanged. The new R3-003 (resolvePoolInnerFields null fallback) compounds this — a undefined-result rpc → null fields → silently empty book.
impact: An aberrant or partial JSON-RPC response (proxy injection, edge-case server impl) results in silent empty data instead of an explicit error.
recommendation: After the env.error branch: `if (env.result === undefined) throw new Error(\`${method} returned no result and no error\`);`.

title: computeMarketStats decoders still unguarded BigInt; Number(quantity) still NaN-poisons depth
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-009. decodeAskPrice/decodeBidPrice still call `BigInt(orderId)` with no try/catch. Iter-4's new console.warn-on-failure path in dataLayer.ts is upstream, but the LIVE fallback path is `decodeAskPrice(o.order_id)` / `decodeBidPrice(o.order_id)` (marketStats.ts lines 49 & 55) — these are reached when dataLayer's price injection fails (the new R3-001 path: console.warn fires, price=undefined, fallback decoder runs). For a SyntaxError-failing order_id, that fallback decoder will ALSO throw SyntaxError synchronously — the error path that iter-4 added a console.warn for is exactly the path that then crashes. Number(o.quantity) on lines 50/56 still has no Number.isFinite guard.
impact: The new console.warn from iter-4 is followed immediately by an unhandled SyntaxError from the marketStats fallback for the same orderIdStr. Net effect: the fix log says 'no more silent swallow', but the actual outcome for a malformed order_id is now: console.warn → uncaught throw → fetchPoolStats rejects → entire pool's card becomes a sentinel via App.tsx's allSettled rescue. So the dashboard for that pool degrades silently with the pool-level error banner showing 'SyntaxError: Cannot convert ... to a BigInt'.
recommendation: Either wrap the marketStats decoders' BigInt calls in try/catch and skip the order, or (cleaner) skip pushing orders with unrecoverable order_id at the dataLayer level so the price-undefined fallback is only reached when the order_id IS parseable but the high bits are non-finite. Also add `Number.isFinite(qty)` guard on quantity coercion.

title: main.tsx (iter-4 buildDeps) — fetch + response.json() still unguarded
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-014. Iter-4 refactored loadManifest into the `buildDeps()` factory closure but did NOT add a try/catch around `await fetch(MANIFEST_URL)` or `await response.json()`. Network failure (offline, dev server crashed mid-session) → raw `TypeError: Failed to fetch`. Malformed JSON in the manifest → raw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token...` directly into App's error UI without any indication this is a manifest-shape problem. The Vite middleware itself (vite.config.ts:32-47) does no parse-validation — it streams the bytes — so a partially-written manifest from a mid-flight `pnpm deploy-all` flows through as malformed JSON.
impact: AC1.1/AC1.2 actionable-error guarantee bypassed in the browser path for both failure modes.
recommendation: Wrap `await response.json()` in try/catch and rethrow as 'Deployment manifest at /localnet.json is not valid JSON: ...'. Wrap fetch() too with similar actionable-error wrapping.

title: iter-4 main.tsx still drops the Vite middleware's per-environment 404 body
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-022 / iter-2 R3-012. The Vite middleware at vite.config.ts:39-45 takes care to compute and emit `{"error": "localnet.json not found at <ABS-DISK-PATH>. Run pnpm deploy-all ..."}` when the disk file is missing. main.tsx's iter-4 buildDeps still throws a fixed message that names neither the disk path nor the original cause; the response body is never read. The middleware did the work, the client throws it away.
impact: AC1.2 'actionable error pointing at the bootstrap recipe' is partially satisfied — the message names `pnpm deploy-all` — but loses the per-environment specificity (the actual disk path the middleware tried). This is the difference between 'I know exactly which file isn't there' and 'something somewhere isn't there'.
recommendation: On `!response.ok`, attempt `const body = await response.json().catch(() => null); throw new Error(body?.error ?? defaultMessage);`. Trivial 3-line change.

title: iter-4 main.tsx — #root null-check still silently no-ops, blank page on failure
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-005. The iter-4 refactor preserved the `if (root) { createRoot(root).render(...) }` guard at the bottom of main.tsx. If document.getElementById('root') returns null (broken index.html, hot-reload race, mismatched id), the SPA silently mounts nothing — blank page, no console error.
impact: Blank page with zero diagnostic. Low because index.html is correct today, but the silent-skip default is the wrong choice for a fatal mounting precondition.
recommendation: `if (!root) throw new Error('main.tsx: #root missing in index.html');`. Or at minimum console.error with a recovery hint.

title: manifest.ts loadManifest still rewrites all fs errors to 'not found'
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-003. The catch around fs.readFile still rewrites EACCES, EISDIR, EMFILE all to 'Deployment manifest not found at <path>'. Original error is dropped — no `cause`, no errno, no console.error. Iter-4 didn't touch this. Affects only Node-side test/CLI tooling (production browser path uses the Vite middleware), but the SAME single-message pattern exists in vite.config.ts:38-45 (untouched in iter-4).
impact: Operator with a permissions issue gets pointed at `pnpm deploy-all`, which won't fix it.
recommendation: Discriminate on `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code`: only claim 'not found' for ENOENT, otherwise emit `Deployment manifest at ${path} unreadable: ${code}` with `{ cause: err }`.

title: manifest.ts loadManifest JSON.parse still unguarded; raw SyntaxError thrown
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-004. `JSON.parse(raw) as unknown` on line 105 has no try/catch. A malformed manifest payload throws raw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ... in JSON at position N` with no path, no bootstrap hint, no actionable message. Iter-4 unchanged.
impact: AC1.2 actionable-error guarantee bypassed for malformed-JSON case in the Node loader.
recommendation: Wrap line 105: `try { return parseManifest(JSON.parse(raw), manifestPath); } catch (err) { if (err instanceof SyntaxError) throw new Error(\`Deployment manifest at ${manifestPath} is not valid JSON: ${err.message}. ${BOOTSTRAP_HINT}\`); throw err; }`.
evidence:
const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as unknown;
  return parseManifest(parsed, manifestPath);

title: traverseBigVector still swallows per-slice fetch errors with bare catch+continue
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-015. The per-slice `try { ... } catch { continue; }` is bare — no error logged, no count kept, no signal. Iter-4 added console.warn calls a few lines down (the new BigInt try/catch) demonstrating the team understood the pattern, but did NOT apply the same console.warn discipline here. If ALL slices fail (RPC down mid-loop), traverseBigVector returns `[]` and the pool's book becomes silently empty — exact same symptom as R3-003 above.
impact: Silent total failure of book reads renders identically to a healthy idle pool. iter-1 R3-005 'silent stub' is structurally back. Inconsistent with iter-4's stated 'no more silent swallow' direction (which only applied to the BigInt try/catch 50 lines down in the same function).
recommendation: Apply the same console.warn pattern iter-4 used for the BigInt try/catch: `} catch (err) { console.warn(\`dataLayer: slice ${slice.objectId} for bigVector ${bigVectorId} failed: ${(err as Error).message}; skipping\`); continue; }`. Track failed-slice count for a 'partial data' indicator.

title: buildQueryEventsFn timestamp 0-fallback still truncates pagination on one bad event
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-017. `Number(j['timestamp'] ?? ev.timestampMs ?? 0)` still defaults to 0 (epoch) on missing/non-numeric fields. The fill is then pushed downstream with timestampMs=0, where fillFetcher's `nowMs - ev.timestampMs > DAY_MS` (line 67) is trivially true for any modern clock, sets `crossedWindow = true`, and HALTS pagination. One malformed event truncates the entire pool's fill stream. Iter-4 untouched.
impact: One bad event per pool truncates that pool's fill stream. Volume24h drops to whatever was collected before the malformed event; sparkline truncates similarly. Silent: PoolCard renders the partial data without indicating it's partial.
recommendation: Either skip the event (if `!Number.isFinite(timestampMs) || timestampMs <= 0`) or default to nowMs so malformed events are treated as 'still in window' and don't trigger crossedWindow.

title: App.tsx setInterval refresh still has no in-flight guard; slow fetches can stack and overlap
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-018. The periodic-refresh effect uses `setInterval(async () => { ... await Promise.allSettled(...) }, 20_000)`. setInterval does NOT wait for the previous callback to resolve before firing. If a fetchPoolStats batch takes >20s (entirely possible with R3-016 unbounded pagination, R3-005 no-timeout fetch, or just slow chain reads), a second batch starts while the first is in flight. Both batches setState; the second-to-resolve overwrites the first. With n pools and slow fetches, in-flight requests stack indefinitely. Iter-4 did not touch.
impact: Under degraded RPC conditions, the SPA accumulates background fetches. Memory/socket pressure on the browser; multiplied RPC load can worsen the sandbox's slowness. setState ordering non-deterministic — user sees stats flicker between fresh and stale.
recommendation: Track in-flight ref: `const inFlightRef = useRef(false); ... if (inFlightRef.current) return; inFlightRef.current = true; try { await ... } finally { inFlightRef.current = false; }`. Or replace setInterval with self-rescheduling setTimeout that fires the next call only after the previous resolves.

title: fetchFills `while (true)` still has no upper-bound iteration cap
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-011. fetchFills uses `while (true)` with three break conditions but no maximum-iteration safety bound. If queryEvents returns hasNextPage:true indefinitely (chain-shape drift, broken cursor advancement, or merely the per-pool filter dropping every event so neither MAX_FILLS nor crossedWindow ever fires), fetchFills hangs forever. Iter-4 unchanged.
impact: Hung loading state with no timeout. Combined with the setInterval refresh (R3-015), a hung fetchFills will block subsequent refresh cycles' Promise.allSettled.
recommendation: Add hard iteration cap: `for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++)` and throw 'queryEvents pagination exceeded N pages without satisfying stop conditions' if reached. Also detect cursor-no-advance.

title: aggregateFills still coerces fill price/quantity via Number() with no NaN guard
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-010. aggregateFills sums `Number(f.baseQuantity)` into volume24h and casts `Number(sorted[last].price)` for lastPrice without guarding NaN. A single malformed fill record poisons the whole day's volume (NaN + N = NaN for the rest of the loop) and lastPrice silently becomes NaN. PoolCard's fmt sentinel masks the symptom — user sees '—' for ALL trades when only one was malformed.
impact: Single bad fill corrupts whole-day volume. Silent: '—' looks identical to 'no trades'. Reachable via the live data layer.
recommendation: `const q = Number(f.baseQuantity); if (Number.isFinite(q)) volume24h += q;` and similarly for price. Optional: count and surface malformedFills in the FillAggregate interface.

title: fetchFills assumes response.data iterable; non-array throws non-actionable TypeError
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-012. `for (const ev of response.data)` will throw `TypeError: response.data is not iterable` if a custom QueryEventsFn (or rpc()'s undefined-result path R3-006) returns `data: undefined`. Iter-4 unchanged.
impact: Edge-case crash with non-actionable error.
recommendation: `if (!Array.isArray(response.data)) throw new Error('queryEvents returned non-array data field');` at top of loop body.
evidence:
for (const ev of response.data) {
      if (ev.poolId !== poolId) continue;

title: App.tsx refresh interval setState still fires after unmount; no cancelled flag
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-019. The setInterval callback calls setState unconditionally on resolution; no `cancelled` ref equivalent to the initial-load effect (line 42). Cleanup clears the interval but a callback already in-flight when cleanup ran will still call setState after unmount. React will warn; in strict-mode dev double-invocation this fires reliably. Iter-4 unchanged.
impact: Console-warning noise + small leak. Pollutes the AC1.1 'no console errors' goal in dev.
recommendation: Add a `cancelled` ref shared across both effects (or a single AbortController) and guard each setState behind `if (!cancelled.current) setState(...)`.

title: runDataLayer still silently coerces missing packageId to empty string
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-021. `const packageId = manifest.packages?.deepbook?.packageId ?? '';` silently coerces missing packageId to '' rather than throwing. Downstream queryEvents call then issues `{ MoveModule: { package: '', module: 'pool' } }` which the Sui RPC rejects — error eventually surfaces as a confusing JSON-RPC error rather than the validated 'manifest missing packages.deepbook.packageId' error parseManifest is designed to throw. Iter-4 unchanged. (Iter-4's main.tsx buildDeps DOES enforce packageId-defined-before-fetchPoolStats with a thrown wiring-bug error — good — but runDataLayer is a separate entry point that bypasses that check.)
impact: Defensive gap. Silent fallback duplicates parseManifest's responsibility but doesn't enforce it.
recommendation: Add explicit assertion at top of runDataLayer: `if (!manifest.packages?.deepbook?.packageId) throw new Error('runDataLayer: manifest missing packages.deepbook.packageId');`. Or change the manifest type to LoadedManifest (the validated shape).
evidence:
const pools = manifest.pools ?? {};
  const packageId = manifest.packages?.deepbook?.packageId ?? '';

title: PoolCard fmt() still uses String(value); fine numerics render as scientific notation
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R3-013. fmt() returns `String(value)` for finite numbers; very small/large values render as scientific notation (e.g. '1.23e-8') which a non-technical user might misread as the sentinel. Iter-4 unchanged. Lower urgency now that R3-002 (bit-127 mask) fix means we're no longer leaking 9.22e+18 garbage into the UI, but the underlying formatting hazard remains.
impact: Cosmetic / latent UX bug. Not load-bearing for any AC.
recommendation: Mirror sparkline's toFixed approach: `value.toLocaleString(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 6 })` or pin per-field toFixed.
